matched_rules.because: A cooling failure occurred and the contingency plan called for switching to standby chillers; the standby chillers shared the same water circulation system as the active chillers, so the failover failed.
Chillers were recirculated and gas discharged but would not restart individually; the site's chillers are configured as a bound cluster, so individual restart will not work until they are unbound.
Mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer; temperatures are rising and approaching safe operational thresholds.
Data center temperatures are increasing and cooling capacity is insufficient; the data center is at risk of exceeding safe operating temperatures.
Cooling system has failed and server room temperatures are rising uncontrollably; temperatures are approaching the level that could trigger the fire sprinkler system.

next_actions.action: Do not assume standby chillers will take over; confirm the standby plant draws from an independent water circuit before relying on it. If the standby shares the same water loop, treat the failover as likely to fail and move directly to auxiliary heat dissipation and ventilation measures. Notify the chiller manufacturer early rather than waiting for the failover to prove ineffective.

Recognize that individual chiller restart will not work while the chillers remain bound into a cluster. Plan to manually modify chiller configurations to unbind them from the cluster so each can be restarted individually. Expect that restarting chillers one after another will slow restoration of the whole cooling system.

Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted. Expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin. Recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.

Progressively decrease the thermal load within the data center space. Consider terminating non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover activities. If thermal load reduction is insufficient, power down servers to prevent an even longer outage and further impact to infrastructure.

Begin reducing loads on computing, storage, network, database, and big data clusters to slow temperature rise. Shut down servers in rooms with high temperature. Treat sprinkler activation as a risk that can damage power supply cabinets and server racks and complicate restoration.

escalate.to: facility operations lead and chiller manufacturer
escalate.reason: Standby chillers confirmed to share the same water circulation system as the failed active chillers (R-007 trigger); chillers will not restart individually and are confirmed bound into a cluster (R-008 trigger); thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started (R-002 trigger); temperatures continue to rise despite initial load reduction (R-006 trigger); temperatures continue to rise despite load reduction and sprinkler activation is possible (R-009 trigger).

not_covered: No rule addresses the specific scenario of a chiller malfunction causing rising corridor temperatures without a preceding utility voltage event or control-system failover.

No rule covers the situation where the data center infrastructure provider's engineers switch to standby chillers and restart based on the contingency plan, but the measures do not take effect, and then auxiliary heat dissipation and ventilation measures are implemented.
No rule addresses the notification of the chiller manufacturer after the issue remains unsolved following multiple attempts.

per_finding.note: No rule or action mentions air entering the cooling system due to lack of water.
R-007 explicitly addresses standby chillers sharing the same water circulation system and failover failure.
R-008 covers chillers bound into a cluster and the need to unbind for individual restart.
R-009 action directs reducing loads on computing, storage, network, database, and big data clusters.
R-008 action includes manually modifying chiller configurations to unbind them from the cluster.
R-009 action treats sprinkler activation as a risk that can damage power supply cabinets and server racks.
R-007 addresses failover effectiveness but does not mention deadlocks or ensuring both automatic and manual failover.
R-006 action includes powering down servers but does not specify standardized emergency processes or when to power off server rooms.
No rule or action mentions expanding monitoring metrics or fine-grained data.
